configKeys.effect: Seconds the glow lasts when no duration is typed (the implicit "infinite"). -1 means Integer.MAX_VALUE ticks (~3.4 years, reported as "indefinitely"); any other value is used as seconds and is NOT checked against max_duration.
Upper bound in seconds for an explicitly typed duration; 0 disables the check. It does not bound the default_duration path, and it does not reject zero or negative durations.
Whether /mobglow needs permission level 2. Read live in the command's requires predicate, so it takes effect without a restart. false opens every subcommand, including "all clear", to every player.

Caps only the number reported in chat and the command's Brigadier return value; 0 means uncapped. It does NOT limit how many mobs actually receive the glow - despite the config comment claiming it does.

events: net.neoforged.neoforge.event.RegisterCommandsEvent (game event bus; NeoForge.EVENT_BUS.register(this) in onInitialize line 71, @SubscribeEvent on onRegisterCommands line 87, which returns early when !isModuleEnabled())
notes:
PROVEN FROM SOURCE (adversarial re-verification of the first pass; vanilla behaviour checked against the decompiled 1.21.1 sources in build/neoForm/neoFormJoined1.21.1-20240808.144430/steps/patchUserDev/output.jar and against brigadier-1.3.10.jar).

FILES (complete module, two classes): modules/mob_glow/MobGlowModule.java and modules/mob_glow/config/MobGlowConfig.java. Nothing else. Plus standalone/mob_glow/MobGlowStandalone.java (@Mod("vpa_mob_glow"), boots via StandaloneModuleBootstrap). Registered in the bundle at VanillaPlusAdditions.java:153 (import at :27); standalone entry at build.gradle:447 with no dataGlobs, no moduleDeps, no mixins and no clientMixins. vanillaplusadditions.mixins.json has no mob_glow entry and there is no mixin/mob_glow/ package. No DeferredRegister, no ModList.isLoaded, no shouldInitialize() override, no compat/ package, no JEI plugin, no Minecraft.getInstance(), no Dist.CLIENT, no KeyMapping -> items/blocks/entities/keybinds/recipes/requiredMods/optionalMods are all genuinely empty and "side": "server" is honest (RegisterCommandsEvent only fires server-side; the glowing outline itself is stock vanilla rendering, so a vanilla client needs nothing installed).

COMMAND SHAPE (MobGlowModule.onRegisterCommands, lines 98-117, the only authoritative source):
- /mobglow <entity_type>              -> executeMobGlowInfinite, i.e. duration literal "infinite"
- /mobglow <entity_type> <duration>   -> duration is a StringArgumentType.word()
- /mobglow <entity_type> clear        -> clears that type
- /mobglow all clear                  -> clears everything this module still tracks
<entity_type> is a ResourceLocationArgument.id(), so a bare "zombie" becomes minecraft:zombie. Tab-completion suggests every ENTITY_TYPE registry key except minecraft:player; applying to players is additionally rejected with "Cannot apply glow effect to players" (clearing is not, but a player can never be in the tracking map anyway).

BRIGADIER SHADOWING (verified by disassembling CommandNode.getRelevantNodes: an exact literal match returns Collections.singleton(literal) and the argument children are never tried):
- /mobglow all      -> only the "all" literal is considered, it has no .executes -> "Unknown or incomplete command". It does NOT fall through to entity_type.
- /mobglow all 30   -> same shadowing, "all" has only the "clear" child -> parse error.
- /mobglow clear    -> "clear" is NOT a literal at the root (only "all" is), so it IS accepted syntactically and parses as the entity type minecraft:clear -> "Unknown entity type: minecraft:clear". (The first pass called this "no bare /mobglow clear"; it is accepted, it just fails with that message.)
- /mobglow <type> clear -> "clear" IS a literal under entity_type, so "clear" can never be read as a duration.

DOC CONTRADICTIONS (important for the doc writer - do not copy these forward):
1. docs/modules/mob_glow.md:20 claims the duration accepts time units ("A number with a time unit (e.g., 10s, 5m, 1h)") and :48 shows `/mobglow minecraft:zombie 30s`. The code does a plain Integer.parseInt(durationStr) at line 238; anything non-numeric except the literal word "infinite" hits NumberFormatException and answers "Invalid duration: 30s. Use a number or 'infinite'". Only bare seconds ("30") and "infinite" work. The documented example is simply broken.
2. docs/modules/mob_glow.md:40 says the config lives in `vanillaplusadditions-server.toml`. It does not. Both the bundle (VanillaPlusAdditions.java:131) and the standalone bootstrap (StandaloneModuleBootstrap.java:45) call registerConfig(ModConfig.Type.COMMON, ...), so the real files are `vanillaplusadditions-common.toml` and `vpa_mob_glow-common.toml`. The section is `[modules.mob_glow]` (ModulesConfig pushes "modules", then the module config pushes the module id).
3. docs/modules/mob_glow.md:42-44 lists only enabled/require_op/debug_logging and silently omits default_duration, max_duration and max_mobs_per_command.
README.md:55 is accurate by comparison (it only claims "configurable duration, including infinite").

max_mobs_per_command DOES NOT LIMIT THE EFFECT. In executeMobGlow the serverLevel.getAllEntities().forEach body calls livingEntity.addEffect(...) and trackedGlowingMobs.put(...) unconditionally for every matching entity (lines 269-279); maxMobs is only consulted inside `if (!hadGlowEffect && (maxMobs == 0 || changedCount.get() < maxMobs))` at line 282, i.e. it caps the reported counter. With the default of 100 and 300 zombies loaded, all 300 glow and the chat says 100. It does have one real side effect: changedCount is also the Brigadier return value (line 325), so `execute store result` / a command block's success count is capped at 100 too. The config comment ("Maximum number of mobs that can be affected per command") promises something the code does not do.

LOADED CHUNKS ONLY, SINGLE DIMENSION ONLY. serverLevel.getAllEntities() is `getEntities().getAll()`, the level's entity lookup - only entities in loaded chunks. Both apply and clear are scoped to `source.getLevel()` (CommandSourceStack.getLevel() already returns a ServerLevel, so the `instanceof ServerLevel` at lines 267/338 is always true). Applying in the Overworld never touches the Nether.

CLEARING SILENTLY DISCARDS OTHER-DIMENSION TRACKING - WORSE THAN A ONE-COMMAND PROBLEM. In clearGlowEffects the `trackedGlowingMobs.remove(mobUUID)` at line 366 sits OUTSIDE the found-entity branch, so an entity that does not resolve in this level is dropped from tracking anyway. On top of that, cleanupDeadReferences(serverLevel) runs at the end of EVERY clear (line 370) and deletes every tracked UUID that serverLevel.getEntity(...) cannot resolve - which includes every mob in another dimension and every mob in an unloaded chunk. So even a type-scoped `/mobglow minecraft:zombie clear` in the Overworld forgets Nether creepers that were glowing, and no /mobglow command can ever clear them again. (The first pass only attributed this to `/mobglow all clear`.)

TRACKING IS RAM-ONLY. trackedGlowingMobs is a plain HashMap field on the module instance, never saved to disk. A server restart loses it, so mobs given a practically-infinite glow before the restart stay glowing and `/mobglow all clear` reports "No glowing entities found to clear". The clear commands only ever touch mobs this module put into the map in this session - glow from a spectral arrow or from /effect is never cleared. Conversely, clearing a tracked mob calls removeEffect(GLOWING) unconditionally, so it also strips a glow that came from somewhere else.

"infinite" IS Integer.MAX_VALUE TICKS, NOT VANILLA'S INFINITE. With the default default_duration = -1 the module sets durationTicks = Integer.MAX_VALUE and its own isInfinite flag, and reports "indefinitely". Vanilla's real infinite marker is MobEffectInstance.INFINITE_DURATION = -1 (isInfiniteDuration() is `duration == -1`), which the module never uses. So the effect is a finite ~2.1 billion ticks (~3.4 years at 20 tps) that ticks down and shows a counting-down number in the HUD instead of the infinity symbol. Practically forever, but not vanilla-infinite.

"infinite" IS NOT EVEN ALWAYS PRACTICALLY INFINITE. With any default_duration other than -1 the branch becomes `durationTicks = configDefault * 20`, isInfinite stays false, and the chat reports "for N seconds" - so the word "infinite" on the command line can mean a finite time. max_duration IS NOT CHECKED ON THAT PATH: the `durationSeconds > maxDuration` guard (lines 241-246) sits only in the numeric branch, so default_duration = 99999 with max_duration = 3600 applies 99999 s unchallenged.

UNVALIDATED ZERO, NEGATIVE AND OVERFLOWING DURATIONS (missed by the first pass).
- StringArgumentType.word() accepts '-' and '+' (verified by disassembling StringReader.isAllowedInUnquotedString: 0-9, A-Z, a-z, _, -, ., +), and Integer.parseInt accepts both signs. The only numeric guard is `durationSeconds > maxDuration`. So `/mobglow minecraft:zombie -5` parses, passes the guard, gives durationTicks = -100, and the chat cheerfully says "for -5 seconds".
- MobEffectInstance.hasRemainingDuration() is `isInfiniteDuration() || duration > 0`, so any duration <= 0 (and != -1) makes tick() return false on the entity's very next tick and the effect is removed immediately - the glow may never be visible at all. `/mobglow <type> 0` behaves the same way.
- `configDefault * 20` (line 234) and `durationSeconds * 20` (line 248) are unguarded int multiplications. default_duration accepts up to Integer.MAX_VALUE, so a large value overflows to a negative tick count (it can never land on exactly -1: 20x is always even). On the numeric path the overflow is normally blocked by max_duration, but max_duration = 0 means "no limit", and then e.g. 999999999 overflows too.

RE-APPLYING A SHORTER DURATION DOES NOT SHORTEN AN EXISTING GLOW. The first pass claimed "addEffect overwrites any weaker existing glow"; that is backwards. LivingEntity.addEffect delegates to MobEffectInstance.update, which at equal amplifier (this module always uses amplifier 0) only assigns the new duration inside `else if (this.isShorterDurationThan(other))`. So after `/mobglow minecraft:zombie` (Integer.MAX_VALUE ticks), a following `/mobglow minecraft:zombie 10` changes nothing: the mobs keep glowing for years, changedCount stays 0 and the chat says "All N minecraft:zombie entities already have glow effect". Only a LONGER duration wins. Use the clear subcommand to shorten, not a second apply.

THE EFFECT INSTANCE: `new MobEffectInstance(MobEffects.GLOWING, durationTicks, 0, false, true)` -> ambient = false, visible = true, and showIcon follows visible, so particles and the HUD icon are both shown. GLOWING has no vanilla immunity (LivingEntity.canBeAffected only special-cases INFESTED/OOZING/POISON+REGENERATION), though another mod can veto via NeoForge's MobEffectEvent.Applicable.

ENABLE/DISABLE IS REGISTRATION-TIME, AND THE FIRST PASS BLAMED THE WRONG CLASS. AbstractModule.shouldInitialize() returns true and MobGlowModule does NOT override it, so AbstractModule.initialize always calls onInitialize() for this module. The real gate in the BUNDLE is ModuleManager.initializeModules (lines 89-107), which rebuilds enabledModules from the config and only calls initialize() on enabled ones - so a module disabled at startup never gets NeoForge.EVENT_BUS.register(this) and its command cannot come back without a restart, not even via `/vpa module enable mob_glow` + /reload. In the STANDALONE jar StandaloneModuleBootstrap.boot calls module.initialize(...) unconditionally, so the listener is always registered and the only gate is the `if (!isModuleEnabled()) return;` at line 88 - there, editing the toml and running /reload does add or remove the command. Either way, once the command is in the dispatcher, flipping the config does not remove it until commands are rebuilt (/reload or restart). require_op, by contrast, is read live inside the `.requires(...)` predicate.

PERMISSIONS. The only gate is the shared `.requires(source -> !getConfig().getRequireOpValue() || source.hasPermission(2))` on the command root, so require_op = false opens every subcommand - including `all clear` - to every player. Two TODOs in the source acknowledge this: "// TODO: Permission check for clearing all (is op for now)" (executeClearAllGlow, line 147) and "// TODO: Permission check for making mobs glow (is op for now)" (executeMobGlow, line 208). Note the bundle's own `/vpa module ...` command is separately hardcoded to hasPermission(2).

DEAD LANG KEYS - IN SIX FILES, NOT ONE. Every `command.vpa.mobglow.*` key is unreferenced: `grep -rn "command.vpa.mobglow" src/main/java/` returns nothing, because all /mobglow chat output is hardcoded Component.literal English. The 14 keys still exist in ALL SIX lang files (cs_cz, de_at, de_de, en_us, es_es, fr_fr = 84 dead entries; en_us.json lines 66-79). The first pass mentioned only en_us and then also claimed "no assets/data resources belong to this module at all", which contradicts itself - these lang entries are the module's only resources (there are no models, textures, data/ recipes or loot tables). HISTORY, AND IT WAS DELIBERATE: commit ae2bca3 (2026-05-08, released as 0.10.3 - CHANGELOG:1312 "Hardcoded Strings in MobGlowModule und DeathCoordinatesModule wurden durch translatable Components ersetzt") converted the module to Component.translatable; commit dbc4787 (2026-05-10, released as 0.12.0 - CHANGELOG:1297 "DeathCoordinatesModule und MobGlowModule: Spieler-/Command-Feedback auf direkte Textausgaben umgestellt") switched it back. The first pass called that an accidental "revert"; the CHANGELOG documents it as an intentional change. The keys were simply not cleaned up. Net effect today: /mobglow output is untranslatable English.

MISC. Non-living entity types parse fine (the registry key exists) but are filtered out by `entity instanceof LivingEntity`, so `/mobglow minecraft:item` answers "No minecraft:item entities found to apply glow effect". ArmorStand is a LivingEntity and therefore a valid target. onCommonSetup only emits a debug log line; it is a lifecycle callback driven by ModuleManager/StandaloneModuleBootstrap, not an event this module subscribes to.
oneLiner: An operator command that puts a glowing outline on every mob of one chosen type in the dimension you are standing in - every creeper, every zombie in the loaded chunks - visible through walls until the time runs out or you clear it again.
shortDescription: Provides a command to make all mobs of a specified type glow for debugging and visualization
